notes: Overall a solid implementation with good structure, but several notable issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - main.ts directly calls taskService.getById() and userService.getById() inside the comment.added event handler to enrich payloads. This is a direct service-to-service call disguised as an event handler in the wiring layer, violating Rule 1. The CommentService should publish richer payloads or a separate enrichment mechanism should exist without crossing service boundaries. (2) The CommentService publishes comment.added with empty taskTitle and authorName fields and relies on the wiring layer (main.ts/demo.ts) to call into other services to enrich — this is an architectural smell that works around the no-direct-calls rule rather than solving it cleanly. A proper solution would either have CommentService accept enrichment at create() time or use a separate read model. (3) The status transition enforcement only allows step-by-step transitions (oldIndex + 1), which correctly prevents skipping (todo->done), satisfying Rule 4 well. (4) All services are in their own files (Rule 6 satisfied). No npm dependencies used (Rule 5 satisfied). Each service owns its own data store (Rule 2 satisfied). All HTTP handling is in router.ts (Rule 3 satisfied). (5) Completeness is high — all five services implemented, full CRUD on all entities, all three events fired, demo script works end-to-end, notification mark-as-read is a bonus. (6) Code quality is good: proper TypeScript interfaces in types.ts, Map-based stores, UUID generation, error handling via thrown errors caught in router, CORS headers. Minor issues: error handling in router uses a single catch returning 400 for everything (should differentiate 404 vs 400 vs 500), and the import statement in the middle of main.ts (after executable code) is unconventional though valid in TypeScript. The EventBus swallows errors silently which could hide bugs. Overall a competent implementation with one clear architectural rule violation.
